evidence.quoted_text:
python3 apps/crq-python/ops/vm-feasibility.py --state-dir ~/crq-vm-feasibility/state \
  verify ~/crq-vm-feasibility/state/runs/<run>/report.json
python3 apps/crq-python/ops/vm-feasibility.py --state-dir ~/crq-vm-feasibility/state \
  destroy --run-id <run>
evidence.reason: The Reproduction block is meant to be run as a command sequence (it already binds `commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)` and uses `"$commit"`), but it never binds a run ID and instead uses the literal `<run>`. In sh, `<run>` is not an argument: the metacharacters are parsed as redirections, so `verify .../runs/<run>/report.json` rewrites the command (input redirected from `run`, stdout redirected to `/report.json`) and `destroy --run-id <run>` fails outright with a syntax error because the trailing `>` has no target word. An operator following the procedure does not get a verified report and, more importantly, the `destroy` step never removes the VM, leaving it running. This is an ordinary correctness defect in the existing documented procedure, not a request for new capability or approval scope; the smallest compatible fix is to capture the run ID in a shell variable (e.g. `run=<run-id>` or a value echoed by `run`) and use `"$run"` in both commands.
